## Detailed Content Summary by Category

### 1. GETTING STARTED GUIDES

**`快速入门/必备软硬件.md`** -- Lists required hardware (EVM kit, USB-TTL module, Type-C cable, optional ethernet/MIPI display) and software (MobaXterm/ADB).

**`快速入门/硬件连接.md`** -- Step-by-step guide: jumper config (RECOV/MASKROM for flash modes), power connection via Type-C 5V, debug UART connection (3.3V TTL). Warns against powering on anti-static bags.

**`快速入门/串口登录.md`** -- Serial parameters: 115200 baud, 8N1, no flow control. Walks through MobaXterm serial setup. Buildroot system auto-login (no password required).

**`快速入门/网络登录.md`** -- SSH login guide. Default static IP: 192.168.1.10. Shows how to configure IP via `/etc/dhcpcd.conf`. Login: root/root. PC must be on same subnet.

**`快速入门/ADB登录.md`** -- USB Type-C ADB setup. Driver installation (DriverAssitant), RKDevTool for ADB binary extraction. Commands: `adb shell`, `adb push/pull`.

**`快速入门/系统信息查看.md`** -- Commands for checking disk (`df -h`), memory (`free -h`), kernel version (`uname -a` shows Linux 6.1.99), CPU info (3x Cortex-A7, ARMv7), partitions (`/proc/partitions`), mount points. Demonstrates sync/reboot.

---

### 2. HARDWARE DESIGN DOCS (Peripherals, Interfaces, GPIO, Pinmux)

**`产品介绍/HD-RK3506G-CORE核心板数据手册.md`** -- **KEY REFERENCE**. Rockchip RK3506G2 processor: 3x Cortex-A7 + 1x Cortex-M0, up to 1.5GHz. Built-in 128MB DDR3, 256MB NAND. 35mm x 35mm stamp-hole module (128 pins). Full pin table with all 128 pins, signal names, default functions, and voltage levels. Supports Linux and RT-Thread. Key peripherals: MIPI DSI 2-lane, LCD RGB888, 2x RMII Ethernet, 2x USB2.0 OTG, SDMMC, 3x SPI, 4x SAI/PDM/SPDIF audio, 4x SARADC (10-bit), 11x PWM, 2x CAN FD, 6x UART, 3x I2C, 86 GPIO, 2x JTAG. Power: 0.3W idle, 0.65W boot, 0.5W at 30% load. Operating temp: -20 to +80C.

**`产品介绍/HD-RK3506-EVM底板数据手册.md`** -- Evaluation board datasheet (92mm x 55mm). Hardware resources: 1x USB2.0 Host, 1x USB Device (Type-C for flashing), 1x RJ45 100Mbps Ethernet, 1x debug UART (TTL), 1x MIPI DSI (24-pin FPC), 1x TF card slot, 1x RTC (footprint present, not soldered), RECOVERY/MASKROM jumpers, 2 LEDs (PWR+RUN), 2x 40-pin expansion headers (J8/J9) with UART, SPI, CAN, FSPI, LCD RGB, ADC, microphone pins. Detailed pinout for both J8 and J9 headers. Includes RM_IO function mapping table.

**`【通用】硬件设计/最小系统设计.md`** -- Minimum system requirements: 5V power, reset button, startup config (SARADC_IN0_BOOT, SARADC_IN1_RECOVER), debug UART0, USB OTG0 for flashing, reset circuit. Boot priority: FSPI > SDMMC > USB/SPI2APB. Reference schematics for Maskrom/Loader jumper circuits and debug UART.

**`【通用】硬件设计/电源系统设计.md`** -- Power input protection (3-stage: discharge tube + varistor, X-cap + inductor + TVS, fuse + diode + bulk cap). Primary supply: SGM61232 (4-28V in, 5V/3A out) or TPS5430DDAR (5.5-36V). Secondary supply: RY3430 or MP2143DJ for 3.3V/1.8V. Critical: core board must power up before base board peripherals (use VCC_3V3 enable).

**`【通用】硬件设计/硬件调试与故障分析.md`** -- Fault analysis guide: short-circuit detection with impedance tables (DDR>5K, 0V9>0.3K, CPU>0.2K, 3V3>10K, 1V8>5K), voltage measurement (DDR=1.36V, 0V9=0.9V, CPU=0.95V, 3V3=3.3V, 1V8=1.8V), power-on waveform verification, ripple testing (<3% peak-to-peak).

**`【通用】硬件设计/UART接口电路设计.md`** -- 6x UART, FIFO 64B, up to 4Mbps. Default: UART0-3. UART0 is debug port, must be exposed. M0/M1 pin variants cannot be used simultaneously. Reference circuit with TVS protection.

**`【通用】硬件设计/CAN接口电路设计.md`** -- 2x CAN FD (CAN 2.0B + CAN FD), 3.3V level. Level shifting circuits for 3.3V-to-5V. External transceiver + 120 ohm termination required.

**`【通用】硬件设计/SPI接口电路设计.md`** -- 3x SPI, max 50MHz, 3.3V. SPI0 default. 22 ohm series resistors recommended on CLK/MOSI/MISO.

**`【通用】硬件设计/I2C接口电路设计.md`** -- 3x I2C, max 1Mbit/s, 3.3V. I2C2 default (has encryption IC at 0x68 -- address conflict warning). Level shifting circuits included.

**`【通用】硬件设计/USB接口电路设计.md`** -- 2x USB2.0 OTG. OTG0 is the firmware flashing port (mandatory). VBUSDET needs 3.3V. Three modes: Host, Peripheral, OTG. Reference circuits for ID/VBUS detection.

**`【通用】硬件设计/RMII接口电路设计.md`** -- 2x RMII Ethernet, 10/100Mbps, 3.3V only. 22 ohm series resistors on TXD/RXD/CLK. MDIO needs external pull-up. PCB layout guidelines for differential pairs.

**`【通用】硬件设计/ADC接口电路设计.md`** -- 2x SARADC (actually 4 channels), 10-bit, 1MS/s, 0-1.8V input. Requires voltage divider for >1.8V. 1nF decoupling cap recommended.

**`【通用】硬件设计/PWM接口电路设计.md`** -- 2 PWM controllers, 12 channels total (11 usable). Supports capture mode, continuous/one-shot modes. IR input/output capability. Configurable via RM_IO.

**`【通用】硬件设计/LCDRGB接口电路设计.md`** -- 1x LCD RGB: 24-bit parallel, 16-bit BT1120, 8-bit BT656 modes. Max 1280x1280@60fps.

**`【通用】硬件设计/MIPIDSI接口电路设计.md`** -- 1x MIPI DSI: 2-lane, V1.2, 1.5Gbps/lane, max 1280x1280@60fps. Direct connection to LCD, no series capacitors.

**`【通用】硬件设计/SAI接口电路设计.md`** -- Up to 4x SAI (Serial Audio Interface), supports PCM/I2S/TDM. Default: SAI1.

**`【通用】硬件设计/DSMC接口电路设计.md`** -- DDR Serial Memory Controller for PSRAM/FPGA. DSMC (master, x8/x16) + DSMC_SLV (slave, x8). Max 150MHz CLK. Pins shared with LCD RGB.

**`【通用】硬件设计/FLEXBUS接口电路设计.md`** -- 2x 16-bit parallel FLEXBUS, max 100MHz. FLEXBUS0 supports CIF camera and QSPI/FSPI. Pins shared with LCD RGB.

**`【通用】硬件设计/FSPI接口电路设计.md`** -- 1x FSPI for NOR/NAND Flash. Only works with eMMC core boards, NOT NAND versions.

**`【通用】硬件设计/SDMMC接口电路设计.md`** -- 1x SDMMC (SDIO3.0 / MMC V4.51). Only for NAND flash core boards, NOT eMMC versions.

**`【通用】硬件设计/ESD_EMI防护设计.md`** -- Comprehensive ESD/EMI protection guidelines: 14 ESD rules (isolation, PCB layout, TVS placement, grounding) and 9+ EMI rules (filtering, shielding, common-mode chokes, heatsink grounding).

---

### 3. PERIPHERAL TESTING GUIDES

**`命令行外设功能测试/HD-RK3506-EVM外设功能测试.md`** -- **COMPREHENSIVE CLI TESTING GUIDE** covering:
- **Ethernet**: ifconfig, static/DHCP IP setup, SSH login (root/root), gateway/route configuration, DNS setup
- **USB flash drive**: auto-mount to `/mnt/udisk`, file copy commands
- **UART testing**: `serial_test` tool with loopback (TX-RX short), 3 additional TTL UARTs at /dev/ttyS1-3
- **ADC testing**: Read via `/sys/bus/iio/devices/iio:device0/in_voltage{2,3}_raw`
- **GPIO testing**: sysfs export/unexport, direction/value control, GPIO number calculation formula (bank*32+num), debug via `/sys/kernel/debug/gpio`
- **LCD display**: DRM/modetest framework, `modetest -M rockchip` to inspect connectors/CRTCs/planes, `modetest -s 75@72:480x800` for color bars
- **Backlight**: `echo 150 > /sys/class/backlight/backlight/brightness` (0-255)
- **RTC/Clock**: date, hwclock, timezone configuration

**`[通用]RK3506应用笔记/PWM输入捕获模式测频率和占空比.md`** -- PWM input capture mode: configure RM_IO12 as PWM0_CH2, use `/sys/class/pwm/pwmchip0/pwm0/capture` to read period and duty cycle in nanoseconds. Verified with signal generator (100Hz, 50% duty).

**`快速入门/RK3506-EVM-AMP/RK3506AMP功能测试.md`** -- **AMP (Asymmetric Multi-Processing) testing**: 3x A7 running Linux + M0 running HAL-MCU. Tests include:
- HAL-UART: M0 UART1 debug output, UART2 data TX/RX loopback
- HAL-GPIO: pull-up/down, output high/low, falling-edge interrupt with callback
- HAL-Timer: 24MHz timer precision, interrupt latency measurement (avg 2633ns, max 19024ns)
- HAL-I2C: I2C2 device scanning (RJGT102 at 0x68)
- RPMSG inter-core communication: pingpong test between A7 Linux and M0 via shared memory + interrupts, max 496 bytes per message

---

### 4. SDK AND BSP INFO

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/SDK编译.md`** -- **SDK compilation reference**. Linux 6.1 SDK (rk3506_linux6.1_sdk_v1.2.0). Directory structure: app, buildroot, device/rockchip, kernel, prebuilts, rkbin, tools, rtos, u-boot. Cross-compiler: gcc-arm-10.3. Board configs: 6 defconfigs for different combos (RK3506B/J/G x IOT/EVM x EMMC/NAND/SD). Full build: `./build.sh`. Partial: `./build.sh kernel`, `./build.sh uboot`, `./build.sh buildroot`. Kernel menuconfig: `make ARCH=arm menuconfig`. Lists all kernel defconfig files and device tree files for each board variant.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/RK3506文件系统buildroot配置手册.md`** -- Buildroot configuration: `make menuconfig` in buildroot dir, architecture Cortex-A7, add packages (e.g. QT5), overlay directory for custom files at `buildroot/board/vanxoak`, permanent save via `make update-defconfig`.

**`快速入门/文件系统.md`** -- Default filesystem: buildroot with ubi_squashfs (read-only). Config file uses `#include` for modular configuration. How to switch to read-write filesystem (requires partition table adjustment). Single package rebuild: `make <pkg>-dirclean && make <pkg>-rebuild`.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/RM_IO.md`** -- **RM_IO Matrix IO system**: 98 functional signals mappable to 32 physical pins. Fully software-configurable via device tree pinctrl subsystem. Design principle: decouple function signals from physical pins. GPIO range: GPIO0_A0-C7, GPIO1_B1-B3, GPIO1_C2-C3, GPIO1_D1-D3.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/GMAC.md`** -- GMAC Ethernet device tree: RMII mode, clock direction, PHY reset GPIO, pinctrl groups, MDIO PHY nodes with 25MHz reference clock. Kernel config, verification steps (ip link, ethtool, ping), troubleshooting checklist.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/CAN.md`** -- CAN FD device tree: compatible "rockchip,rk3506-canfd", 300MHz clock, RM_IO pinmux. Classic CAN and CAN FD config examples (`ip link set can0 type can bitrate 500000 dbitrate 2000000 fd on`). can-utils testing (candump/cansend). Hardware: external transceiver + 120 ohm termination.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/UART.md`** -- UART device tree: pinctrl for RX/TX via RM_IO, status "okay". Kernel: CONFIG_SERIAL_8250. Test: minicom/picocom. Hardware flow control (RTS/CTS) optional extension.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/I2C.md`** -- I2C device tree: clock-frequency 400kHz, RTC example (RS4C1339 at 0x68, compatible "dallas,ds1339"). Debug: i2cdetect, dmesg, hwclock.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/SPI.md`** -- SPI device tree: spidev test device on SPI0, max 50MHz. Kernel: CONFIG_SPI_SPIDEV, CONFIG_SPI_ROCKCHIP. Test: `spidev_test -D /dev/spidev0.0`.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/显示触摸驱动移植.md`** -- **Display/touch driver porting** for both RGB and MIPI screens. RGB: panel device tree with display-timings (clock, resolution, porches, sync), backlight PWM, GT911 touch on I2C0. MIPI: DSI panel with init command sequences (0x05/0x15/0x39 command types), lane-rate, CST128A touch on I2C2. Detailed guide on converting vendor init code to device tree format.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/RK3506OTA升级.md`** -- OTA upgrade via Recovery mode. UpdateEngine tool: supports SD/USB/network (HTTP) upgrade. Partition-level or full system upgrade. Network flow: download, verify MD5, flash, reboot to recovery, apply, reboot. Also includes shell script for application-only upgrade via USB.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/SD启动卡制作.md`** -- SD boot card creation: erase NAND/eMMC first, use SDDiskTool_v1.78 (Windows), select SD boot mode + update.img, write to >=8GB SD card. Verified on HD-RK3506-EVM.

**`SDK开发与外设设备树配置/Logo的制作与替换.md`** -- Boot logo: BMP format, 24-bit, resolution <= display. Replace `logo.bmp` / `logo_kernel.bmp` in kernel build dir, rebuild `./build.sh kernel`, flash boot.img.

---

## 4. Structure of a Typical ARM64 Chip Port

Based on the RK3399 port (the simplest ARM64 chip port) and comparison with the richer imx9 port:

### Minimal Chip Directory (`arch/arm64/src/<chip>/`)

```
arch/arm64/src/rk3399/
    chip.h                      # Chip header (minimal, includes nuttx/config.h)
    Kconfig                     # Peripheral Kconfig menu (UART, GPIO, etc.)
    Make.defs                   # Build rules: include common/Make.defs + CHIP_CSRCS
    <chip>_boot.c               # CRITICAL: MMU config, arm64_el_init(), arm64_chip_boot()
    <chip>_boot.h               # Declares <chip>_board_initialize()
    <chip>_serial.c             # UART driver (early serial + full serial)
    <chip>_serial.h             # UART addresses, IRQ numbers
    <chip>_lowputc.S            # Assembly low-level console output (for early boot)
    hardware/
        <chip>_memorymap.h      # Peripheral base addresses
```

### Key Functions a Chip Port Must Provide

1. **`arm64_el_init()`** -- Called very early from `arm64_head.S` at high EL; for clock/security init
2. **`arm64_chip_boot()`** -- Main chip boot: MMU init, PSCI init, board init, serial init
3. **`<chip>_board_initialize()`** -- Board-specific init hook
4. **`arm64_earlyserialinit()`** -- Early UART setup for debug console
5. **`arm64_serialinit()`** -- Register serial devices (`/dev/console`, `/dev/ttyS0`, etc.)
6. **`arm64_lowputc()`** -- Assembly-level character output for boot debugging
7. **`up_putc()`** -- C-level character output
8. **MMU region table** -- `g_mmu_regions[]` defining device and DRAM memory regions

### How the Build System Integrates a Chip

In `arch/arm64/Kconfig`:
```
config ARCH_CHIP_RK3399
    bool "Rockchip RK3399"
    select ARCH_CORTEX_A53
    ...
config ARCH_CHIP
    default "rk3399" if ARCH_CHIP_RK3399
...
if ARCH_CHIP_RK3399
source "arch/arm64/src/rk3399/Kconfig"
endif
```

The chip's `Make.defs` must include `common/Make.defs` and define `CHIP_CSRCS` / `CHIP_ASRCS`.

## 5. Vendor Template and Example Board Structure

### Vendor Template (`vendor/template/`)

Located at `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/vendor/template/`. This is the **official template** for creating new vendor ports. It uses placeholder names:

- `vendor_name` -- e.g., "rockchip"
- `chip_name` -- e.g., "rk3576"
- `board_name` -- e.g., "kickpi-k7"

#### Template Chip Directory (`chips/chip_name/`)

```
chips/chip_name/
    chip.h                              # Chip header
    Kconfig                             # Uses ARCH_CHIP_CUSTOM, defines ARCH_CHIP_CHIP_NAME
    Make.defs                           # Includes arch Make.defs, lists CHIP_CSRCS
    CMakeLists.txt                      # CMake build support
    vendor_name_start.c                 # __start() -> nx_start()
    vendor_name_start.h                 # Start header
    vendor_name_irq.c                   # IRQ handling
    vendor_name_irq.h                   # IRQ numbers (NR_IRQS, NVIC config)
    vendor_name_uart.c                  # Serial driver stub
    vendor_name_lowputc.h               # Low-level putc header
    vendor_name_oneshot.c               # Timer/oneshot driver
    vendor_name_allocateheap.c          # Heap allocation
    include/
        chip.h                          # Public chip header
        irq.h                           # Public IRQ header
```

#### Template Board Directory (`boards/chip_name/board_name/`)

```
boards/chip_name/board_name/
    Kconfig                             # Board Kconfig (empty template)
    CMakeLists.txt                      # CMake build
    include/
        board.h                         # Board header
        nsh_romfsimg.h                  # ROMFS image for init scripts
    src/
        Makefile                        # Board source build rules
        CMakeLists.txt                  # CMake build
        board_name.h                    # Board header
        vendor_name_ap.c                # board_app_initialize(), board_late_initialize(), bringup()
        etc/
            group                       # /etc/group
            init.d/
                rc.sysinit              # Init script
                rcS                     # Shell startup script
    scripts/
        Make.defs                       # Toolchain and linker script config
        ld.script                       # Linker script (MEMORY, SECTIONS)
    configs/
        nsh/defconfig                   # Default NSH configuration
        refconfig_ap_Wearable_ARMV8M    # Reference configs for various use cases
        refconfig_BLE_Only
        refconfig_BLE_WIFI
        ...
```

#### Usage (from `REMEDE.md`):

```bash
# 1. Copy template
cp -r template rockchip

# 2. Run rename script
cd rockchip
python rename.py rockchip kickpi-k7 rk3576

# 3. Clean up
rm rename.py REMEDE.md .git

# 4. Build
./build.sh vendor/rockchip/boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/configs/nsh -j8
```

### Vendor vs. Main Tree Approach

There are **two paths** for adding a new chip:

1. **Main NuttX tree** (`nuttx/arch/arm64/src/<chip>/`): For upstream/community chips. Requires adding to `nuttx/arch/arm64/Kconfig` and `nuttx/boards/Kconfig`.

2. **Vendor tree** (`vendor/<vendor>/chips/<chip>/` and `vendor/<vendor>/boards/<chip>/<board>/`): For proprietary/vendor-specific chips. Uses `ARCH_CHIP_CUSTOM` and `ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM` Kconfig options. The vendor template at `vendor/template/` provides the scaffolding.

The RK3399 is in the main tree. The RK3576 is being set up in the vendor tree (currently README-only).

## Summary: What You Need to Port a New Rockchip ARM64 Chip

For a new Rockchip chip (e.g., RK3506 or RK3576), you would need:

### Option A: Main NuttX Tree (like RK3399)

1. **Create** `nuttx/arch/arm64/src/rk3576/` with:
   - `chip.h`, `Kconfig`, `Make.defs`
   - `rk3576_boot.c` (MMU regions, `arm64_el_init()`, `arm64_chip_boot()`)
   - `rk3576_serial.c` + `rk3576_serial.h` (UART driver)
   - `rk3576_lowputc.S` (early boot console)
   - `hardware/rk3576_memorymap.h` (peripheral addresses)

2. **Create** `nuttx/boards/arm64/rk3576/<boardname>/` with:
   - `Kconfig`, `include/board.h`, `src/`, `scripts/`, `configs/nsh/defconfig`

3. **Register** in `nuttx/arch/arm64/Kconfig` (add `ARCH_CHIP_RK3576` choice + source line)

4. **Register** board in `nuttx/boards/Kconfig`

### Option B: Vendor Tree (like the RK3576 template)

1. Copy `vendor/template/` to `vendor/rockchip/` (already exists)
2. Run `rename.py` to replace placeholders
3. Implement chip-level code in `vendor/rockchip/chips/rk3576/`
4. Implement board-level code in `vendor/rockchip/boards/rk3576/<boardname>/`
5. Uses `ARCH_CHIP_CUSTOM` / `ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM` -- no changes to main NuttX tree needed

### 方案 B：移植 openvela 到 HD-RK3506-EVM（全新移植）

**RK3506G2 芯片特性**：
- 3x Cortex-A7（1.5GHz）+ 1x Cortex-M0
- 内置 128MB DDR3
- 丰富外设：6x UART, 3x SPI, 3x I2C, 2x CAN FD, 2x USB OTG, 2x RMII 以太网, MIPI DSI, LCD RGB, 4x SAI 音频, 11x PWM, 4x SARADC

**移植路径选择**：

| 路径 | 位置 | 优势 | 劣势 |
|------|------|------|------|
| **主干 NuttX 树** | `nuttx/arch/arm64/src/rk3506/` | 社区维护，与主分支同步 | 需要社区审核 |
| **Vendor 目录** | `vendor/rockchip/chips/rk3506/` | 自主控制，不影响主干 | 需手动同步更新 |

**推荐使用 Vendor 目录方式**（参考 `vendor/template/` 模板）。

### 移植步骤（方案 B 详细）

#### 第 1 步：芯片层适配（Chip Layer）

创建 `vendor/rockchip/chips/rk3506/`：

```
rk3506/
├── chip.h                    # 芯片头文件
├── include/
│   ├── chip.h                # 公共芯片头文件
│   └── irq.h                 # 中断定义
├── Kconfig                   # 芯片配置项（UART/定时器等）
├── Make.defs                 # 编译源文件列表
├── rk3506_start.c            # __start() 入口函数
├── rk3506_irq.c              # 中断处理
├── rk3506_serial.c           # UART 驱动（基于 DesignWare 8250）
├── rk3506_lowputc.S          # 早期控制台输出
├── rk3506_timeisr.c          # 定时器驱动
├── rk3506_allocateheap.c     # 堆内存初始化
└── hardware/
    └── rk3506_memorymap.h    # 外设基地址
```

**关键实现**：

1. **启动入口** `__start()`：
   - 清除 BSS 段
   - 拷贝 .data 段
   - 初始化系统时钟
   - 初始化串口（UART0 为调试串口）
   - 调用 `nx_start()`

2. **UART 驱动**（参考 RK3399 的 `rk3399_serial.c`）：
   - RK3506 使用 DesignWare 8250 兼容 UART
   - 6 路 UART，FIFO 64 字节，最高 4Mbps
   - UART0 默认为调试串口

3. **定时器**：推荐使用 `arch_alarm` 模型（单次定时器）

4. **中断系统**：实现 `up_irq_initialize()`、`up_enable_irq()`、`up_disable_irq()` 等

5. **内存管理**：
   - RK3506G 内置 128MB DDR3
   - 计算堆起始地址：`ebss + CONFIG_IDLETHREAD_STACKSIZE`
   - 堆大小：`RAM 末地址 - 起始地址`

#### 第 2 步：板级层适配（Board Layer）

创建 `vendor/rockchip/boards/rk3506/hd-rk3506-evm/`：

```
├── include/
│   ├── board.h               # 板级定义（时钟、GPIO 等）

│   ├── Makefile

│   ├── hd_rk3506_appinit.c   # 应用初始化
│   ├── hd_rk3506_bringup.c   # 外设启动
│   └── etc/
│       ├── group
│       └── init.d/
│           ├── rc.sysinit

├── scripts/
```

### RM_IO 引脚复用系统

RK3506 的核心特性是 **RM_IO（Matrix IO）** 系统：
- 98 个功能信号可映射到 32 个物理引脚
- 完全通过设备树 pinctrl 子系统软件配置
- 设计原则：功能信号与物理引脚解耦

例如，将 RM_IO12 配置为 PWM0_CH2：
```c
&pinctrl {
    pwm0_ch2_pin: pwm0-ch2-pin {
        rockchip,pins = <1 RK_PB3 3 &pcfg_pull_none>;
    };
};
```

### 外设驱动适配优先级

| 优先级 | 外设 | openvela 支持情况 | 难度 |
|--------|------|------------------|------|
| P0 | UART（调试串口） | 已有框架，参考 RK3399 | 低 |
| P0 | GPIO | 已有框架 | 低 |
| P1 | I2C | 已有框架 | 中 |
| P1 | SPI | 已有框架 | 中 |
| P1 | 定时器 | arch_alarm 框架 | 中 |
| P2 | CAN FD | 需要新驱动 | 中 |
| P2 | 以太网 (RMII) | 需要 MAC+PHY 驱动 | 高 |
| P2 | PWM | 已有框架 | 中 |
| P3 | USB | 需要 EHCI/OHCI 驱动 | 高 |
| P3 | 显示 (MIPI/RGB) | 需要 LCDC 驱动 | 高 |
| P3 | 音频 (SAI) | 需要 I2S 驱动 | 高 |

### AMP 异构多核方案

RK3506 支持 AMP（非对称多处理），可参考 HD-RK3506 文档中的方案：

| 方案 | A7 核心 | M0 核心 | 适用场景 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| 方案 1 | 3x Linux | M0 HAL-MCU | 通用 Linux + 实时控制 |
| 方案 2 | 2x Linux | 1x RT-Thread + M0 HAL | 多 RTOS 混合 |
| 方案 3 | 2x Linux | 1x RT-Thread | 双 RTOS |
| 方案 4 | 1x Linux | 1x Bare-metal + 1x RT-Thread | 最大实时性 |

**openvela 方案建议**：
- A7 核心运行 openvela（替代 Linux）
- M0 核心运行 HAL-MCU 做实时控制
- 通过 RPMSG 共享内存 + 中断实现核间通信

## 一、40Pin LCD 5寸 800x480 + GT911 触摸

### 接口类型判断

40pin 800x480 LCD 通常是 **RGB 并行接口**（RGB565/RGB888）。HD-RK3506-EVM 的 **J8 扩展口** 正好引出了 LCD RGB 信号。

### 硬件接线

J8 扩展口的 LCD 相关引脚：

| J8 Pin | 信号 | 功能 | LCD 40pin 对应 |
|--------|------|------|---------------|
| 27 | VO_LCDC_HSYNC | 行同步 | HSYNC |
| 28 | VO_LCDC_VSYNC | 场同步 | VSYNC |
| 29 | VO_LCDC_D23 | 数据位 RGB888 高位 | R7/R5 |
| 30 | VO_LCDC_CLK | 像素时钟 | PCLK/DCLK |
| 31 | VO_LCDC_D21 | 数据位 | R5/R3 |
| 32 | VO_LCDC_D22 | 数据位 | R6/R4 |
| 33 | VO_LCDC_D19 | 数据位 | R3/G7 |
| 34 | VO_LCDC_D20 | 数据位 | R4/G0 |
| 35-38 | J9 扩展口 | LCD D1-D7 | G1-G5, B0-B2 |

**注意**：完整 RGB888 需要 24 根数据线，但 J8/J9 只引出了部分。如果你的 5 寸屏是 **RGB565**（16 位），则只需 16 根数据线 + HSYNC + VSYNC + PCLK + DE = 20 根信号线。

### GT911 触摸接线

GT911 通过 **I2C** 连接，参考 HD-RK3506 文档中的配置：

| 信号 | 连接到 | 说明 |
|------|--------|------|
| SDA | I2C0_SDA (RM_IO) | I2C 数据线 |
| SCL | I2C0_SCL (RM_IO) | I2C 时钟线 |
| INT | GPIO (任意空闲) | 触摸中断引脚 |
| RST | GPIO (任意空闲) | 复位引脚 |
| VCC | 3.3V | 供电 |
| GND | GND | 地 |

GT911 的 I2C 地址通常是 **0x5D**（INT 拉高时）或 **0x14**（INT 拉低时）。

### openvela 驱动支持

**好消息**：openvela 已有完整的 GT911 触摸驱动实现。

参考文件：
- `nuttx/boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-box/src/esp32s3_board_touchsceen_gt911.c` — 完整的 GT911 驱动（450 行），通过 I2C 读取触摸点，注册为 `/dev/inputN` 触摸设备

关键寄存器：
```c
#define GT911_READ_XY_REG     0x814e   // 触摸状态寄存器
#define GT911_READ_DATA_REG   0x814f   // 触摸数据寄存器
#define GT911_CONFIG_REG      0x8047   // 配置寄存器
#define GT911_PRODUCT_ID_REG  0x8140   // 产品 ID
```

### Kconfig 配置

```kconfig
# I2C 支持
CONFIG_I2C=y

# 触摸屏输入框架
CONFIG_INPUT=y
CONFIG_INPUT_TOUCHSCREEN=y

# LCD Framebuffer（如果使用 framebuffer 模式）
CONFIG_LCD=y
CONFIG_LCD_FRAMEBUFFER=y
CONFIG_LCD_RGB565=y   # 或 RGB888
```

## 二、0.96 寸 SPI 屏幕

0.96 寸屏幕通常是以下两种之一：

| 类型 | 分辨率 | 驱动芯片 | 接口 |
|------|--------|----------|------|
| OLED | 128x64 | SSD1306 | I2C 或 SPI |
| TFT | 160x80 或 128x160 | ST7735 / ST7789 | SPI |

### 硬件接线（J9 扩展口 SPI0）

| J9 Pin | 信号 | 屏幕引脚 | 说明 |
|--------|------|----------|------|
| 14 | SPI0_CSN0 | CS | 片选 |
| 15 | SPI0_MISO | MISO/SDO | 数据输入（可选） |
| 16 | SPI0_MOSI | MOSI/SDA/SCL | 数据输出 |
| 17 | SPI0_CLK | CLK/SCK | 时钟 |
| 1 | VCC3P3 | VCC | 3.3V 供电 |
| 22/39/40 | GND | GND | 地 |

**额外 GPIO**（需要额外 2 根线）：
- **DC**（数据/命令选择）— 接任意空闲 GPIO
- **RST**（复位）— 接任意空闲 GPIO（或接高电平）

### openvela 驱动支持

openvela 已内置以下 SPI LCD 驱动：

| 驱动 | 文件 | Kconfig |
|------|------|---------|
| **SSD1306** (OLED) | `drivers/lcd/ssd1306_spi.c` / `ssd1306_i2c.c` | `CONFIG_LCD_SSD1306` |
| **ST7735** (TFT) | `drivers/lcd/st7735.c` | `CONFIG_LCD_ST7735` |
| **ST7789** (TFT) | `drivers/lcd/st7789.c` | `CONFIG_LCD_ST7789` |

### SSD1306 OLED 配置示例

```kconfig
CONFIG_LCD=y
CONFIG_LCD_SSD1306=y
CONFIG_LCD_SSD1306_SPI=y        # SPI 模式
CONFIG_SSD1306_SPIMODE=0        # SPI Mode 0
CONFIG_SSD1306_FREQUENCY=10000000  # 10MHz
CONFIG_SSD1306_XRES=128
CONFIG_SSD1306_YRES=64
```

板级初始化代码：
```c
#include <nuttx/spi/spi.h>
#include <nuttx/lcd/ssd1306.h>

void board_lcd_init(void)
{
  FAR struct spi_dev_s *spi;
  FAR struct lcd_dev_s *lcd;
  struct ssd1306_priv_s priv = {
    .devno = 0,
  };

  /* 获取 SPI 设备 */
  spi = spibus_initialize(0);  /* SPI0 */

  /* 初始化 SSD1306 */
  lcd = ssd1306_initialize(spi, &priv, 0);

  /* 注册 framebuffer */
  lcd_register(lcd, 0);
}
```

## 三、两个屏幕同时使用

两个屏幕可以同时工作，因为它们使用不同的总线：

| 屏幕 | 总线 | 资源 |
|------|------|------|
| 5 寸 RGB LCD | LCD 并行接口 | VOP + LCDC 控制器 |
| 0.96 寸 SPI 屏 | SPI0 | SPI 控制器 |

**注意**：RK3506 的 VOP（显示控制器）同时只能驱动一个显示输出（MIPI DSI 和 LCD RGB 二选一）。如果用 RGB LCD，就不能同时用 MIPI DSI。

### 完整 Kconfig 配置建议

```kconfig
# === 显示 ===
CONFIG_LCD=y
CONFIG_LCD_FRAMEBUFFER=y
CONFIG_LCD_RGB565=y          # 5寸 RGB LCD

# === 0.96寸 SPI 屏（二选一） ===
# CONFIG_LCD_SSD1306=y       # OLED
# CONFIG_LCD_ST7735=y        # TFT
# CONFIG_LCD_ST7789=y        # TFT

# === 触摸 ===
CONFIG_INPUT=y
CONFIG_INPUT_TOUCHSCREEN=y
CONFIG_I2C=y

# === SPI ===
CONFIG_SPI=y
CONFIG_SPI_EXCHANGE=y

# === Framebuffer 支持 ===
CONFIG_VIDEO_FB=y
CONFIG_FB_CMAP=y
```

## 4. RGB Parallel LCD vs SPI LCD - How They Are Driven

### SPI LCD Panels (e.g., ST7789, ILI9341, SSD1306)

The LCD driver **owns the pixel transfer**. The pipeline is:

```
Application -> NX/LVGL -> lcd_dev_s.putrun()/putarea() -> SPI bus -> LCD controller GRAM
```

- The LCD controller has its own internal GRAM (Graphics RAM)
- Data is sent serially over SPI (or I2C) to the controller
- The LCD driver implements `struct lcd_dev_s` with `putrun()`/`putarea()` callbacks
- `putrun()` writes a horizontal run of pixels to the controller's GRAM
- `putarea()` writes a rectangular region (optimized bulk transfer)
- **Performance bottleneck**: SPI bandwidth limits refresh rate for larger displays

### Parallel/MCU-Bus LCD Panels (e.g., SSD1289, RA8875)

Similar to SPI but faster data path:

```
Application -> NX/LVGL -> lcd_dev_s.putrun()/putarea() -> 8080/6800 parallel bus -> LCD controller GRAM
```

- Uses memory-mapped 8-bit or 16-bit parallel bus
- Same `lcd_dev_s` interface as SPI drivers
- Significantly faster than SPI but still command/data based

### RGB/Parallel Interface LCD Panels (e.g., connected to SoC LCD controller)

**Critical distinction**: RGB interface panels are **NOT driven by `drivers/lcd/` drivers**. As noted in `ili9341.c` line 78-80:

> "Note! RGB interface will not be supported by the lcd driver. It should be used with the platform specific RGB graphic controller and the nuttx framebuffer interface."

RGB panels are driven through a **completely different path**:

```
Application -> NX/LVGL -> fb_vtable_s -> SoC LCD controller (LTDC/DCMI/etc.) -> RGB bus -> Panel
```

- The SoC has a dedicated LCD controller (e.g., STM32 LTDC, Rockchip VOP) with DMA
- The controller scans framebuffer memory and drives HSYNC/VSYNC/DATA lines directly
- No GRAM on the panel - pixels are streamed in real-time
- The `fb_vtable_s` implementation is **board/SoC-specific** (not in `drivers/lcd/`)
- The framebuffer memory is typically in external SDRAM, memory-mapped
- Examples: `goldfish_fb.c`, `goldfish_gpu_fb.c`, or vendor-specific drivers in `vendor/`

## 5. LCD Framebuffer Frontend (`CONFIG_LCD_FRAMEBUFFER`)

**File**: `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/drivers/lcd/lcd_framebuffer.c`

This is the **bridge** that makes any LCD driver appear as a standard framebuffer device. It is the key architectural component.

### How it works:

1. `up_fbinitialize(display)` is called during boot
2. It calls `board_lcd_initialize()` + `board_lcd_getdev()` to get the `lcd_dev_s` instance
3. It allocates a RAM framebuffer (`fbmem`) of size `xres * yres * bpp / 8`
4. It creates a `fb_vtable_s` that wraps the LCD driver
5. The vtable's `updatearea()` method copies the relevant portion of the RAM framebuffer to the LCD via `putarea()` or `putrun()`

### Key data structure:

```c
struct lcdfb_dev_s {
  struct fb_vtable_s vtable;        // Framebuffer vtable (wraps LCD)
  FAR struct lcd_dev_s *lcd;        // The underlying LCD driver
  FAR uint8_t *fbmem;               // Allocated RAM framebuffer
  FAR struct lcd_planeinfo_s pinfo; // LCD plane info (bpp, putrun, putarea)
  size_t fblen;                     // Framebuffer size in bytes
  fb_coord_t xres, yres;           // Resolution
  fb_coord_t stride;                // Row stride in bytes
};
```

### Update flow:

```
Application writes to /dev/fb0 (mmap or write)
  -> fb.c:fb_write()/fb_mmap() modifies RAM framebuffer
  -> FBIO_UPDATE ioctl
  -> lcdfb_updateearea()
    -> pinfo->putarea() or row-by-row pinfo->putrun()
      -> SPI/parallel transfer to LCD controller GRAM
```

### Board integration APIs:

Defined in `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/board.h`:

```c
int board_lcd_initialize(void);                    // Init LCD hardware
FAR struct lcd_dev_s *board_lcd_getdev(int lcddev); // Get LCD device instance
void board_lcd_uninitialize(void);                 // Cleanup
FAR struct lcd_dev_s *board_graphics_setup(unsigned int devno); // External init
```

## 6. LVGL Integration Points

LVGL connects to NuttX through **two alternative paths**, selected via Kconfig:

### Path A: LCD Character Device (`CONFIG_LCD_DEV`)

This is the **recommended path for LVGL** (as stated in the Kconfig help text):

> "This option enables support for a character driver which exposes LCD operations to userspace via ioctl() commands. This is useful when not using NXGraphics but an alternative graphics library such as LVGL."

```
LVGL -> /dev/lcd0 (ioctl: LCDDEVIO_PUTAREA, LCDDEVIO_GETAREA)
  -> lcd_dev.c:lcddev_ioctl()
    -> lcd_planeinfo_s.putarea()/getarea()
      -> LCD hardware
```

Key ioctls for LVGL (from `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/lcd/lcd_dev.h`):
- `LCDDEVIO_PUTRUN` - Write a row of pixels
- `LCDDEVIO_PUTAREA` - Write a rectangular area
- `LCDDEVIO_GETRUN` / `LCDDEVIO_GETAREA` - Read back pixels
- `LCDDEVIO_GETVIDEOINFO` - Get display resolution/format
- `LCDDEVIO_GETPLANEINFO` - Get bpp, stride, etc.
- `LCDDEVIO_SETPOWER` / `LCDDEVIO_GETPOWER` - Backlight control
- `LCDDEVIO_GETAREAALIGN` - Get alignment requirements

### Path B: Framebuffer Device (`CONFIG_LCD_FRAMEBUFFER`)

```
LVGL -> /dev/fb0 (mmap + FBIO_UPDATE ioctl)
  -> fb.c -> lcd_framebuffer.c -> LCD hardware
```

Or with direct framebuffer (RGB panels):
```
LVGL -> /dev/fb0 (mmap, direct write, FBIO_UPDATE)
  -> fb.c -> SoC LCD controller -> RGB panel
```

Key ioctls for LVGL (from `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/video/fb.h`):
- `FBIOGET_VIDEOINFO` - Get xres, yres, format
- `FBIOGET_PLANEINFO` - Get fbmem, fblen, stride, bpp
- `FBIO_UPDATE` - Trigger display refresh (for LCD framebuffer frontend)
- `FBIO_WAITFORVSYNC` - Wait for vsync
- `FBIOSET_POWER` - Backlight control
- `FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO` / `FBIOGET_FSCREENINFO` - Linux-compatible screen info

### Two fundamentally different hardware models:

**Model 1: Smart LCD (SPI/I2C/Parallel MCU bus)**
- LCD controller has its own GRAM
- Data sent command-by-command over serial/parallel bus
- NuttX uses `lcd_dev_s` interface (`putrun`/`putarea`)
- Optionally wrapped by `lcd_framebuffer.c` for `/dev/fbN` access
- Performance limited by bus bandwidth

**Model 2: Dumb RGB Panel (RGB/Parallel display interface)**
- Panel has no internal memory
- SoC LCD controller DMA-scans framebuffer memory to drive RGB signals
- NuttX uses `fb_vtable_s` interface directly
- Board/SoC-specific driver provides the vtable implementation
- No `drivers/lcd/` involvement at all
- High performance, GPU-accelerated possible

## 5. Network Stack Integration -- How USB Network Devices Connect to TCP/IP

The NuttX network stack defines link-layer types in `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/net/net.h`:

```c
NET_LL_ETHERNET = 0,
NET_LL_LOOPBACK,
NET_LL_SLIP,
NET_LL_TUN,
NET_LL_BLUETOOTH,
NET_LL_IEEE80211,
NET_LL_IEEE802154,
NET_LL_PKTRADIO,
NET_LL_MBIM,       // CDC-MBIM USB host driver
NET_LL_CAN,
NET_LL_CELL        // Cellular Virtual Network Device
```

**USB network device integration flow** (using CDC-MBIM as the example):

1. The USB host class driver (`usbhost_cdcmbim.c`) creates a `struct net_driver_s`
2. It registers callbacks: `d_ifup`, `d_ifdown`, `d_txavail`
3. It calls `netdev_register(&priv->netdev, NET_LL_MBIM)` to register with the NuttX network stack
4. Packets are received via USB bulk IN transfers and pushed to the network stack
5. Outgoing packets are pulled via `d_txavail` and sent via USB bulk OUT transfers

**Key files:**
- `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/drivers/usbhost/usbhost_cdcmbim.c` (2480 lines) -- USB host CDC-MBIM network driver
- `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/net/netdev/netdev_register.c` -- Network device registration (line 386-387: MBIM case)
- `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/net/netlink/netlink_route.c` -- Netlink routing (MBIM handling, line 307)
- `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/drivers/net/netdev_upperhalf.c` -- Netdev upper half (MBIM case, line 755)

### E27-A 与 RK3506 的连接方式

**通过 USB 连接**（经过 SL2.1A Hub）：

```
RK3506 USB OTG (Host)
    │
    ▼
SL2.1A USB Hub
    │
    ├── Port 1 ──→ E27-A USB (从模式)
    │               → 枚举为 CDC-ACM 设备
    │               → /dev/ttyACM0 (AT 指令通道)
    │
    └── Port 2 ──→ RTL8723DU USB
                    → WiFi + BT
```

E27-A 通过 USB 枚举为 **CDC-ACM 虚拟串口**，openvela 的 `usbhost_cdcacm.c` 驱动会自动识别并创建 `/dev/ttyACM0`。

### E27-A 联网 AT 指令流程

```
# 1. 检查 SIM 卡
AT+CPIN?
→ +CPIN: READY

# 2. 查询信号强度
AT+CSQ
→ +CSQ: 20,99

# 3. 查询网络注册
AT+CREG?
→ +CREG: 0,1

# 4. 设置 APN (根据运营商)
AT+CGDCONT=1,"IP","cmnet"      # 中国移动
AT+CGDCONT=1,"IP","3gnet"      # 中国联通
AT+CGDCONT=1,"IP","ctnet"      # 中国电信

# 5. 激活 PDP 上下文
AT+CGACT=1,1

# 6. 拨号上网 (PPP)
ATD*99***1#
→ CONNECT

# 或者使用 Q 指令直接建立 TCP 连接:
AT+QIOPEN=1,0,"TCP","220.181.38.148",80,0,1
AT+QISEND=0,5
> Hello
```

openvela 中通过 PPPD + Chat 实现自动拨号：

```
ABORT 'NO CARRIER'
ABORT 'ERROR'
'' AT
OK AT+CPIN?
OK AT+CSQ
OK AT+CGDCONT=1,"IP","cmnet"
OK ATD*99***1#
CONNECT \c
```

## 快应用框架是否在本次移植范围内？

### 快应用框架现状

openvela 已有完整的快应用框架，位于 `frameworks/runtimes/quickapp/`：

| 组件 | 说明 | 依赖 |
|------|------|------|
| **QuickJS 引擎** | 轻量级 JS 引擎 | 独立，无特殊依赖 |
| **Feature 框架** | JS-Native 互操作 (JIDL) | C/C++ 运行时 |
| **应用 Shell** | 快应用容器/运行时 | 框架层 |
| **快应用 IDE** | 开发工具 (AIoT-IDE) | PC 端 |

### 快应用的核心依赖

```
快应用运行需要：
├── QuickJS 引擎            ✅ 纯软件，无硬件依赖
├── 框架 Feature API         ✅ 纯软件
├── 图形显示                 ⚠️ 依赖 LVGL 或 NX 图形栈
├── 输入设备                 ⚠️ 依赖触摸/按键驱动
├── 网络能力                 ⚠️ 依赖网络栈 (WiFi/4G)
├── 文件系统                 ✅ 已有
└── 存储 (Flash/SD)          ⚠️ 依赖存储驱动
```

### 建议：分阶段纳入

| 阶段 | 是否包含快应用 | 理由 |
|------|--------------|------|
| Phase 1 (芯片层) | **否** | 先确保系统能启动 |
| Phase 2 (显示) | **否** | 先跑 LVGL 验证显示 |
| Phase 3 (USB/网络) | **否** | 先验证 4G 联网 |
| Phase 4 (WiFi/BT) | **可选** | 网络就绪后可尝试 |
| **Phase 5 (系统集成)** | **是** | 所有基础设施就绪后集成 |

### 快应用集成的 defconfig 配置

```kconfig
# 快应用框架
CONFIG_QUICKAPP=y
CONFIG_QUICKAPP_LOG_LEVEL=0
CONFIG_QUICKAPP_VAPP=y

# 依赖的图形栈
CONFIG_GRAPHICS_LVGL=y
CONFIG_LV_USE_NUTTX=y

# 依赖的网络栈
CONFIG_NET=y
CONFIG_NET_TCP=y
CONFIG_NET_UDP=y

# 依赖的文件系统
CONFIG_FS_ROMFS=y
CONFIG_FS_TMPFS=y
```

### 结论

**快应用框架建议纳入 Phase 5（系统集成阶段）**，理由：

1. **快应用本身是纯软件框架**，对硬件无直接依赖，理论上只要 openvela 系统跑起来就能用
2. **但它依赖图形栈 + 网络栈 + 输入设备**，这些需要在 Phase 1-4 先就绪
3. **快应用的优势**是开发效率高（JS 写 UI），适合做产品原型和演示
4. **如果目标是"把 OpenVela 所有功能搞上"**，那快应用确实应该包含在内

```c
  and \tmp1, \tmp1, #3
  ldr \tmp2, =g_irqstack_top
  lsls \tmp1, \tmp1, #2
  add \tmp2, \tmp2, \tmp1
  ldr sp, [\tmp2, #0]
  .endm
#endif
```

#### 4c. `Kconfig` -- Core Selection Pattern

In the top-level `arch/arm/Kconfig`, your chip must select the core:

```kconfig
config ARCH_CHIP_YOURCHIP
    bool "Your SoC Name"
    select ARCH_CORTEXA7                    # Selects ARCH_ARMV7A + MMU + caches + FPU + MPCore
    select ARM_HAVE_NEON                    # If applicable
    select ARCH_HAVE_LOWVECTORS             # Typical for SDRAM-booted chips
    select ARCH_HAVE_SDRAM
    depends on BOOT_RUNFROMSDRAM
    select ARCH_HAVE_ADDRENV
    select ARCH_NEED_ADDRENV_MAPPING
```

Then in your chip's `Kconfig`:
```kconfig
if ARCH_CHIP_YOURCHIP

config YOURCHIP_UART0
    bool "UART 0"
    default y
    select UART0_SERIALDRIVER
    select ARCH_HAVE_SERIAL_TERMIOS

# Select armv7-a features your SoC has:
config ARCH_CHIP_YOURCHIP_VARIANT
    bool
    select ARMV7A_HAVE_GICv2         # If GICv2
    select ARMV7A_HAVE_GTM           # If global timer
    select ARMV7A_HAVE_PTM           # If private timer
    select ARMV7A_HAVE_L2CC_PL310    # If PL310 L2 cache

endif # ARCH_CHIP_YOURCHIP
```

#### 5b. Linker Script Pattern

From `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/boards/arm/am335x/beaglebone-black/scripts/sdram.ld`:

```ld
MEMORY
{
    isram (W!RX) : ORIGIN = 0x402F0400, LENGTH = 63K
    ocmc0 (W!RX) : ORIGIN = 0x40300000, LENGTH = 64K - 16K   /* 16K reserved for page table */
    ddr   (W!RX) : ORIGIN = 0x8a000000, LENGTH = 512M - 160M
}

ENTRY(entry)
ENTRY(_stext)

SECTIONS
{
    .text :
    {
        _stext = ABSOLUTE(.);
        *(.vectors)                    /* <-- Vector table first */
        *(.text .text.*)
        *(.rodata .rodata.*)
        // ... ARM exception tables (.ARM.extab, .ARM.exidx) ...
        _etext = ABSOLUTE(.);
    } > ddr

    .data : { _sdata = ABSOLUTE(.); ... _edata = ABSOLUTE(.); } > ddr
    .bss  : { _sbss = ABSOLUTE(.);  ... _ebss = ABSOLUTE(.);  } > ddr
}
```

### 6. UART/Serial Driver Pattern

There is **no generic 8250/DW UART driver** in the armv7-a chips. Each chip implements its own serial driver. However, for QEMU-based chips, the **PL011 driver** is used as a reusable driver at `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/drivers/serial/`.

For a custom UART driver, the pattern is (from `am335x_serial.c`):

```c
#include <nuttx/serial/serial.h>

// 1. Define private device structure
struct up_dev_s
{
  uint32_t uartbase;   /* Base address */
  uint32_t baud;
  uint32_t ier;        /* Saved IER */
  uint8_t  irq;
  uint8_t  parity;
  uint8_t  bits;
  bool     stopbits2;
};

// 2. Implement uart_ops_s callbacks
static int  up_setup(struct uart_dev_s *dev);
static void up_shutdown(struct uart_dev_s *dev);
static int  up_attach(struct uart_dev_s *dev);
static void up_detach(struct uart_dev_s *dev);
static int  up_ioctl(struct file *filep, int cmd, unsigned long arg);
static int  up_receive(struct uart_dev_s *dev, unsigned int *status);
static void up_rxint(struct uart_dev_s *dev, bool enable);
static bool up_rxavailable(struct uart_dev_s *dev);
static void up_send(struct uart_dev_s *dev, int ch);
static void up_txint(struct uart_dev_s *dev, bool enable);
static bool up_txready(struct uart_dev_s *dev);
static bool up_txempty(struct uart_dev_s *dev);

static const struct uart_ops_s g_uart_ops =
{
  .setup       = up_setup,
  .shutdown    = up_shutdown,
  .attach      = up_attach,
  .detach      = up_detach,
  .ioctl       = up_ioctl,
  .receive     = up_receive,
  .rxint       = up_rxint,
  .rxavailable = up_rxavailable,
  .send        = up_send,
  .txint       = up_txint,
  .txready     = up_txready,
  .txempty     = up_txempty,
};

// 3. Per-port buffers and state
static char g_uart0rxbuffer[CONFIG_UART0_RXBUFSIZE];
static char g_uart0txbuffer[CONFIG_UART0_TXBUFSIZE];

static struct up_dev_s g_uart0priv =
{
  .uartbase = YOUR_UART0_BASE_ADDR,
  .baud     = CONFIG_UART0_BAUD,
  .irq      = YOUR_UART0_IRQ,
  .parity   = CONFIG_UART0_PARITY,
  .bits     = CONFIG_UART0_BITS,
  .stopbits2 = CONFIG_UART0_2STOP,
};

static uart_dev_t g_uart0port =
{
  .recv = { .size = CONFIG_UART0_RXBUFSIZE, .buffer = g_uart0rxbuffer },
  .xmit = { .size = CONFIG_UART0_TXBUFSIZE, .buffer = g_uart0txbuffer },
  .ops  = &g_uart_ops,
  .priv = &g_uart0priv,
};

// 4. Register with NuttX
void arm_earlyserialinit(void) { ... }
void arm_serialinit(void) { up_register(&g_uart0port, ...); }
```

If your Cortex-A7 SoC has a **PL011 or NS16550-compatible UART**, you can reuse the existing drivers from `drivers/serial/` (goldfish uses PL011, for example).

## 方案对比

| 方案 | 难度 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| **A. U-Boot 网络加载** | 低 | 保留原有 Linux，通过 U-Boot TFTP 加载 nuttx.bin |
| **B. U-Boot SD 卡加载** | 低 | 将 nuttx.bin 放入 SD 卡，U-Boot 从 SD 卡加载 |
| **C. 替换 boot.img** | 中 | 将 nuttx.bin 打包成 boot.img，替换原 Linux 内核 |
| **D. 完整打包** | 高 | 打包成 update.img，包含 bootloader + nuttx + romfs |

## 推荐：方案 B (U-Boot SD 卡加载)

最快验证方式，不需要修改原有固件：

### 步骤 1: 准备 SD 卡

```
SD 卡根目录放置:
├── nuttx.bin      # 编译产物
└── boot.scr       # U-Boot 启动脚本 (需生成)
```

### 步骤 2: 生成 U-Boot 启动脚本

```bash
# 创建 boot.cmd
cat > boot.cmd << 'EOF'
# openvela NuttX boot script
setenv nuttx_addr 0x02080000
fatload mmc 1:1 ${nuttx_addr} nuttx.bin
go ${nuttx_addr}
EOF

# 生成 boot.scr (需要 mkimage 工具)
mkimage -A arm -O linux -T script -C none -a 0 -e 0 -n "openvela" -d boot.cmd boot.scr
```

### 步骤 3: 从 SD 卡启动

1. 将 SD 卡插入开发板
2. 上电，U-Boot 自动加载 `boot.scr`
3. `boot.scr` 执行 `fatload` 加载 `nuttx.bin` 到 `0x02080000`
4. `go 0x02080000` 跳转执行 openvela
5. 调试串口 (UART0) 输出 NSH Shell

## 方案 A: U-Boot 网络加载 (TFTP)

如果开发板有网络连接：

```bash
# 在 U-Boot 命令行中执行
setenv serverip 192.168.1.100    # TFTP 服务器 IP
setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.10       # 开发板 IP
tftp 0x02080000 nuttx.bin
go 0x02080000
```

## 方案 C: 替换 boot.img

将 nuttx.bin 包装成 Rockchip boot.img 格式：

```bash
# 使用 Rockchip 的 mkbootimg 工具
mkbootimg --kernel nuttx.bin \
          --base 0x02080000 \
          --kernel_offset 0x00000000 \
          --output boot.img

# 然后用 RKDevTool 单独烧录 boot.img 分区
```

## RK3506 Linux SDK: NAND Flashing Process and Firmware Packaging Analysis

### 1. Boot Flow: ROM -> SPL -> U-Boot -> Kernel

The RK3506 uses a standard Rockchip boot chain. Here's the complete flow:

**Boot ROM (Internal)**
- The RK3506 has an internal Boot ROM that runs on power-on
- It looks for boot media (SPI NAND, eMMC, SD card) based on boot pin configuration
- For NAND: Boot ROM loads the SPL (Secondary Program Loader) from the NAND flash

**SPL (MiniLoaderAll.bin)**
- The SPL is built from two components, defined in `/home/b4qaq/project/RK3506G2/rk3506_linux6.1_sdk_v1.2.0_iot_evm/rkbin/RKBOOT/RK3506MINIALL.ini`:
  - `FlashData`: `bin/rk35/rk3506_ddr_750MHz_v1.06.bin` (DDR initialization)
  - `FlashBoot`: `bin/rk35/rk3506_spl_v1.11.bin` (SPL code)
- The SPL initializes DDR RAM, then loads U-Boot
- The combined loader binary is generated as `rk3506_spl_loader_v1.06.111.bin`
- An IDB (ID Block) image is also generated: `rk3506_idblock_v1.06.111.img`

**U-Boot**
- Configured via `RK_UBOOT_CFG_FRAGMENTS="rk3506b rk3506_tb"` (for NAND variants)
- The `rk3506b.config` fragment at `/home/b4qaq/project/RK3506G2/rk3506_linux6.1_sdk_v1.2.0_iot_evm/u-boot/configs/rk3506b.config` sets `CONFIG_LOADER_INI="RK3506BMINIALL.ini"` and `CONFIG_BASE_DEFCONFIG="rk3506_defconfig"`
- The `rk3506_tb.config` fragment enables Thunder Boot (`CONFIG_SPL_KERNEL_BOOT=y`) which allows SPL to directly boot the kernel without full U-Boot
- U-Boot produces `uboot.img` and `trust.img` (OP-TEE TEE at address 0x1000)
- For NAND: `CONFIG_SPL_MTD_SUPPORT=y`, `CONFIG_MTD_SPI_NAND=y`, `CONFIG_ROCKCHIP_SFC=y`

**Thunder Boot Mode**
- The NAND defconfigs use `RK_BOOT_FIT_ITS_NAME="thunderboot.its"` at `/home/b4qaq/project/RK3506G2/rk3506_linux6.1_sdk_v1.2.0_iot_evm/device/rockchip/.chips/rk3506/thunderboot.its`
- In Thunder Boot mode, SPL directly loads the kernel FIT image (kernel + DTB) without full U-Boot
- Kernel is loaded at `0x01100000`, DTB at `0x00063000`

### 5. Boot.img Format

**boot.img is a FIT (Flattened Image Tree) image**

For NAND with Thunder Boot, the boot.img is created using the `thunderboot.its` at `/home/b4qaq/project/RK3506G2/rk3506_linux6.1_sdk_v1.2.0_iot_evm/device/rockchip/.chips/rk3506/thunderboot.its`:
- Contains: kernel image + DTB (device tree blob)
- Kernel load address: `0x01100000`
- DTB load address: `0x00063000`
- No ramdisk (for normal boot)
- The `thunderboot4recovery.its` adds a ramdisk at `0x01800000`

The FIT image is created by `mk-fitimage.sh` at `/home/b4qaq/project/RK3506G2/rk3506_linux6.1_sdk_v1.2.0_iot_evm/common/scripts/mk-fitimage.sh`:
```bash
"$RK_SDK_DIR/rkbin/tools/mkimage" -f "$TMP_ITS" -E -p 0x800 "$TARGET_IMG"
```

**Can nuttx.bin be used as the kernel in boot.img?**
- Yes, in principle. The FIT image format is flexible - it can contain any binary payload
- You would need to:
  1. Create a custom .its file that references nuttx.bin as the kernel payload
  2. Set the correct load/entry addresses for your NuttX binary
  3. Use `rkbin/tools/mkimage` to create the FIT image
- However, the RK3506 boot ROM expects a specific IDB (ID Block) format for the initial SPL loader, so you'd still need the Rockchip DDR init binary and SPL

### 7. NAND Boot Partition Layout

**Standard NAND Layout** (`parameter-iot-nand.txt` / `parameter-evm-nand.txt`):
```
Partition    Offset (sectors)  Size (sectors)  Size (human)
---------    ----------------  --------------  -----------
vnvm         0x00000800        0x00001000      2MB (NVM/OTP data)
uboot        0x00001800        0x00004000      8MB (U-Boot + SPL)
misc         0x00005800        0x00001000      2MB (boot flags)
recovery     0x00006800        0x0000f000      30MB (recovery kernel)
boot         0x00015800        0x00005000      10MB (kernel FIT image)
rootfs       0x0001a800        0x00050000      160MB (UBIFS rootfs)
oem          0x0006a800        0x00008000      16MB (OEM data)
userdata     0x00072800        - (grow)        Remaining space
```

**Partition format**: `CMDLINE:mtdparts=:SIZE@OFFSET(NAME),...`
- Sizes and offsets are in sectors (512 bytes each)
- The `:grow` suffix means the partition expands to fill remaining space
- The `vnvm` partition stores non-volatile memory data (MAC addresses, etc.)

**eMMC Layout** (`parameter-iot-emmc.txt`) for comparison:
```
uboot        0x00004000        0x00002000      4MB
misc         0x00006000        0x00002000      4MB
boot         0x00008000        0x00020000      64MB
recovery     0x00028000        0x00040000      128MB
rootfs       0x00068000        0x00c00000      3GB (ext4)
oem          0x00c68000        0x00040000      128MB
userdata     0x00ca8000        - (grow)        Remaining space
```

**Key difference**: NAND uses UBI/UBIFS for rootfs (flash-friendly), while eMMC uses ext4. NAND has a `vnvm` partition that eMMC doesn't have.

### Complete Workflow: nuttx.bin -> NAND-Flashable Firmware

1. **Build NuttX** to produce `nuttx.bin` (ARM Cortex-A7, bare-metal binary)

2. **Create a custom .its file** (similar to `thunderboot.its`):
   - Set kernel image to point to your nuttx.bin
   - Set correct load/entry addresses matching your NuttX linker script
   - Include a DTB if needed (or use a minimal one)

3. **Create the FIT boot image**:
   ```bash
   rkbin/tools/mkimage -f custom.its -E -p 0x800 boot.img
   ```

4. **Prepare the partition table** (`parameter.txt`):
   - Use one of the existing NAND parameter files as a template
   - Adjust partition sizes as needed

5. **Get the SPL loader**:
   - Use the prebuilt `MiniLoaderAll.bin` from `output/firmware/` or build from U-Boot
   - This contains the DDR init code and SPL - you cannot replace this with NuttX

6. **Package the firmware**:
   - Place all images in a directory following the `package-file` format
   - Use `afptool -pack ./ update.raw.img`
   - Use `rkImageMaker -RK3506 MiniLoaderAll.bin update.raw.img update.img`

7. **Flash to NAND**:
   - **Via USB (recovery mode)**: `rkflash.sh all` (uses `upgrade_tool`)
   - **Via update.img**: `rkflash.sh update` (uses `upgrade_tool uf`)
   - **Individual partitions**: `rkflash.sh boot boot.img` etc.

**Important Note**: The RK3506 boot ROM requires the Rockchip-specific SPL format (IDB block with DDR init). You cannot replace MiniLoaderAll.bin with NuttX - the boot ROM won't recognize it. However, you CAN replace the Linux kernel in boot.img with NuttX, as long as the SPL can load and execute it at the correct address.

## 2. DWC2 Register Layout (Based on STM32 Driver)

The DWC2 (DesignWare Core 2) OTG controller uses a well-defined register map. The STM32 driver accesses these via `STM32_OTGFS_BASE + offset`. For RK3506, you simply change the base address.

### 2.1 Register Map Summary

**File:** `/home/b4qaq/project/openvela/nuttx/arch/arm/src/stm32/hardware/stm32fxxxxx_otgfs.h`

#### Core Global Registers (offset 0x000-0x03C)

| Offset | Register | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| 0x000 | GOTGCTL | OTG Control and Status (session request, HNP, connector ID) |
| 0x004 | GOTGINT | OTG Interrupt (debounce done, session change) |
| 0x008 | GAHBCFG | AHB Configuration (global interrupt mask, burst length) |
| 0x00C | GUSBCFG | USB Configuration (PHY select, turnaround time, force host/device mode) |
| 0x010 | GRSTCTL | Reset Register (core soft reset, FIFO flush, AHB idle) |
| 0x014 | GINTSTS | Core Interrupt Status |
| 0x018 | GINTMSK | Core Interrupt Mask |
| 0x01C | GRXSTSR | Receive Status Debug Read |
| 0x020 | GRXSTSP | Receive Status Pop (read-and-pop for host RxFIFO) |
| 0x024 | GRXFSIZ | RxFIFO Size (in 32-bit words) |
| 0x028 | HNPTXFSIZ | Host Non-Periodic Tx FIFO Size |
| 0x02C | HNPTXSTS | Non-Periodic Tx FIFO/Queue Status |
| 0x038 | GCCFG | General Core Configuration (power down, VBUS sensing) |
| 0x03C | CID | Core ID |

#### Host Mode Registers (offset 0x400-0x5F0)

| Offset | Register | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| 0x400 | HCFG | Host Configuration (FS/LS PHY clock select) |
| 0x404 | HFIR | Host Frame Interval |
| 0x408 | HFNUM | Host Frame Number |
| 0x410 | HPTXSTS | Host Periodic Tx FIFO/Queue Status |
| 0x414 | HAINT | Host All Channels Interrupt |
| 0x418 | HAINTMSK | Host All Channels Interrupt Mask |
| 0x440 | HPRT | Host Port Control and Status (connect, enable, reset, speed, power) |

#### Host Channel Registers (offset 0x500 + n*0x20)

For each channel n (0-7 in STM32, typically 0-15 or more on DWC2 variants):

| Offset | Register | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| 0x500+n*0x20 | HCCHAR(n) | Channel Characteristics (maxpacket, epnum, direction, type, device address, speed, enable/disable) |
| 0x504+n*0x20 | HCSPLT(n) | Channel Split (for HS hubs, not used in FS-only) |
| 0x508+n*0x20 | HCINT(n) | Channel Interrupt (XFRC, CHH, STALL, NAK, ACK, TXERR, BBERR, DTERR) |
| 0x50C+n*0x20 | HCINTMSK(n) | Channel Interrupt Mask |
| 0x510+n*0x20 | HCTSIZ(n) | Channel Transfer Size (xfersize, packet count, data PID) |

#### Data FIFO (offset 0x1000 + n*0x1000)

| Offset | Register | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| 0x1000+n*0x1000 | DFIFO(n) | Data FIFO for channel/endpoint n (32-bit read/write window) |

#### Power and Clock Gating (offset 0xE00)

| Offset | Register | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| 0xE00 | PCGCCTL | Power and Clock Gating Control |

## 3. How to Initialize DWC2 in Host Mode

The initialization sequence is implemented in `stm32_hw_initialize()` (line 5285) and `stm32_host_initialize()` (line 5114).

### 3.1 Hardware Initialization Sequence (`stm32_hw_initialize`)

```
Step 1: Select PHY
  - Set GUSBCFG.PHYSEL = 1 (FS serial transceiver)

Step 2: Wait for AHB Idle
  - Poll GRSTCTL.AHBI DL until set (with timeout)

Step 3: Core Soft Reset
  - Write GRSTCTL.CSRST = 1
  - Poll GRSTCTL.CSRST until cleared
  - Wait 3 PHY clocks

Step 4: Deactivate Power-Down
  - Set GCCFG.PWRDWN = 1 (turn on PHY power)
  - Set GCCFG.VBUSASEN | GCCFG.VBUSBSEN (VBUS sensing)
  - Wait 20ms

Step 5: Force Host Mode
  - Set GUSBCFG.FHMOD = 1 (force host mode)
  - Clear GUSBCFG.FDMOD
  - Wait 50ms for mode switch

Step 6: Call stm32_host_initialize()
```

### 3.2 Host Mode Initialization (`stm32_host_initialize`)

```
Step 1: Restart PHY Clock
  - Write 0 to PCGCCTL

Step 2: Configure Host
  - Set HCFG.FSLSPCS = FS48MHz (full-speed PHY clock)

Step 3: Reset Host Port
  - Set HPRT.PRST = 1, wait 20ms
  - Clear HPRT.PRST, wait 20ms

Step 4: Configure FIFO Memory
  - GRXFSIZ = RXFIFO_SIZE (e.g., 128 words = 512 bytes)
  - HNPTXFSIZ = start_address | (NPTXFIFO_SIZE << 16)
  - HPTXFSIZ  = start_address | (PTXFIFO_SIZE << 16)

Step 5: Flush All FIFOs
  - GRSTCTL = TXFFLSH | TXFNUM_HALL, poll until done
  - GRSTCTL = RXFFLSH, poll until done

Step 6: Clear Channel Interrupts
  - For each channel: HCINT(n) = 0xFFFFFFFF, HCINTMSK(n) = 0

Step 7: Drive VBUS
  - Set HPRT.PPWR = 1 (port power)
  - Wait 200ms for VBUS stabilization

Step 8: Enable Host Interrupts
  - Clear all pending: GINTSTS = 0xFFFFFFFF, GOTGINT = 0xFFFFFFFF
  - Enable: RXFLVL | IPXFR | HPRT | HC | DISC | WKUP | USBSUSP
  - Set GAHBCFG.GINTMSK = 1 (global interrupt mask)
```

### 3.3 Software Initialization (`stm32_sw_initialize`)

```
1. Wire up usbhost_driver_s function pointers
2. Initialize hub port structure (drvr, ep0, speed=FULL)
3. Initialize device address generator (usbhost_devaddr_initialize)
4. Set state machine to SMSTATE_DETACHED
5. Initialize all channel semaphores (nxsem_init)
```

### 3.4 Interrupt Registration and Enable

```c
irq_attach(RK3506_IRQ_USB_OTG0, rk3506_gint_isr, NULL);
up_enable_irq(RK3506_IRQ_USB_OTG0);
```

## 4. How USB Enumeration Works

### 4.1 Connection Detection Flow

```
USB Device Plugged In
  -> DWC2 sets HPRT.PCDET (Port Connect Detected)
  -> DWC2 fires GINTSTS.HPRT interrupt
  -> stm32_gint_hprtisr() reads HPRT
     -> Detects PCDET bit
     -> Calls stm32_portreset(priv) -- reset port (20ms assert, 20ms deassert)
     -> Calls stm32_gint_connected(priv)
        -> Sets priv->connected = true
        -> Sets priv->change = true
        -> Posts priv->pscsem (wake up waiter thread)
```

### 4.2 Waiter Thread Flow

```
usbhost_waiter thread loop:
  1. CONN_WAIT(conn, &hport)
     -> stm32_wait() blocks on priv->pscsem
     -> When woken, checks priv->change
     -> Returns hport with connected/disconnected state

  2. If connected:
     CONN_ENUMERATE(conn, hport)
       -> stm32_enumerate()
          -> stm32_rh_enumerate():
             a. Wait 100ms (USB spec: >= 50ms after connection)
             b. stm32_portreset() -- reset port again
             c. Read HPRT.PSPD to get device speed (LS/FS/HS)
             d. Allocate EP0 control channels (stm32_ctrlchan_alloc)
                - Allocate OUT channel for SETUP/OUT packets
                - Allocate IN channel for IN packets
                - Configure both with epno=0, EPTYPE_CTRL, maxpacket=8
          -> usbhost_enumerate(hport, &devclass):
             a. EP0 already configured with default address 0, maxpacket 8
             b. GET_DESCRIPTOR (Device) -- get first 8 bytes (min maxpacket)
             c. EP0 reconfigure with actual maxpacket from descriptor
             d. SET_ADDRESS -- assign unique address
             e. EP0 reconfigure with new address
             f. GET_DESCRIPTOR (Device) -- full 18 bytes
             g. GET_DESCRIPTOR (Configuration) -- full config descriptor
             h. Parse class/subclass/protocol from descriptors
             i. usbhost_findclass() -- find matching registered class driver
             j. CLASS_CREATE(reg, hport, id) -- create class instance
             k. CLASS_CONNECT(devclass, configdesc, desclen) -- bind class
          -> On failure: call stm32_gint_disconnected() to reset state

  3. If disconnected:
     -> CLASS_DISCONNECTED(devclass) if class was bound
     -> Free all channels, reset state to DETACHED
```

### 4.3 Data Transfer Flow

**Control Transfer (ctrlin):**
```
stm32_ctrlin():
  for retries = 0..2:
    1. stm32_ctrl_sendsetup():
       - Set chan->pid = PID_SETUP
       - Set chan->buffer = req (8-byte setup packet)
       - stm32_chan_waitsetup() -- prepare to wait
       - stm32_transfer_start():
         * HCTSIZ = buflen | (1 << PKTCNT) | PID_SETUP
         * HCCHAR |= CHENA (start channel)
         * Write setup packet to DFIFO
       - stm32_chan_wait() -- block on channel semaphore

    2. stm32_ctrl_recvdata() (if buflen > 0):
       - Set chan->pid = PID_DATA1
       - Set chan->buffer = buffer, chan->buflen = buflen
       - stm32_transfer_start()
       - stm32_chan_wait()
       - Data arrives via RxFIFO interrupt -> stm32_gint_rxflvlisr()

    3. stm32_ctrl_senddata() for status phase:
       - Send ZLP with toggled data PID
       - stm32_chan_wait()
```

**Bulk/Interrupt Transfer:**
```
stm32_transfer():
  if IN:
    stm32_in_transfer():
      loop while xfrd < buflen:
        stm32_in_setup() -- set PID, start transfer
        stm32_chan_wait() -- block
        if NAK: retry with delay, timeout after 5s
        update buffer pointer, xfrd count
  else:
    stm32_out_transfer():
      similar pattern for OUT direction
```

### 4.4 Interrupt Processing Chain

```
stm32_gint_isr() -- top-level ISR, loops while pending interrupts:
  |
  +-> GINT.RXFLVL -> stm32_gint_rxflvlisr()
  |     Read GRXSTSP for channel number, byte count, packet status
  |     If INRECVD: read data from DFIFO into buffer, toggle data toggle
  |     If more packets expected: re-activate channel
  |
  +-> GINT.NPTXFE -> stm32_gint_nptxfeisr()
  |     TxFIFO has space: write more OUT data to DFIFO

  +-> GINT.PTXFE -> stm32_gint_ptxfeisr()
  |     Same for periodic (interrupt/isoc) endpoints
  |
  +-> GINT.HC -> stm32_gint_hcisr()
  |     Read HAINT to find which channels have interrupts
  |     For each: read HCCHAR to get direction

  |     OUT: stm32_gint_hcoutisr() -- handle XFRC, NAK, STALL, TXERR, NYET, DTERR, CHH
  |     On transfer complete (XFRC -> CHH): set result=OK, post channel semaphore
  |
  +-> GINT.HPRT -> stm32_gint_hprtisr()
  |     Handle port connect/detect, enable change, speed detection

  +-> GINT.DISC -> stm32_gint_discisr()
```

## 5. Changes Needed to Adapt STM32 Driver for RK3506

### 5.1 Strategy: Copy-and-Modify (Strategy A from HCD Pattern)

The DWC2 IP is identical between STM32 and RK3506. The changes are platform-level: base address, PHY, clock, IRQ, and GPIO.

### 5.2 Specific Changes Required

#### 5.2.1 Register Base Address

| Item | STM32 | RK3506 |
|------|-------|--------|
| OTG0 base | `STM32_OTGFS_BASE` (varies by chip, e.g. 0x50000000) | `0xFF740000` |
| OTG1 base | N/A (single controller) | `0xFF780000` |
| USB2 PHY | Integrated in DWC2 | Separate at `0xFF2B0000` |

Create a new register header file `hardware/rk3506_dwc2.h`:
```c
#define RK3506_DWC2_OTG0_BASE  0xFF740000
#define RK3506_DWC2_OTG1_BASE  0xFF780000
#define RK3506_USB2PHY_BASE    0xFF2B0000

// All register offsets are identical to STM32 -- reuse the offset defines
// Just change the base address macro
#define RK3506_DWC2_GOTGCTL  (RK3506_DWC2_OTG0_BASE + 0x0000)
// ... etc.
```

#### 5.2.2 Number of Host Channels

| Item | STM32 | RK3506 DWC2 |
|------|-------|-------------|
| Host channels | 8 | 12 or 16 (check TRM) |

Change `STM32_NHOST_CHANNELS` to match RK3506 DWC2 hardware parameter. Read GNPTXSTS or HW capability register to determine dynamically if possible.

#### 5.2.3 PHY Initialization

This is the biggest difference. STM32 has an integrated FS PHY; RK3506 has a separate USB2 PHY block.

```c
// NEW: RK3506 USB2 PHY initialization
static void rk3506_usb2phy_init(uint32_t phy_base)
{
  // 1. Enable PHY clock (via CRU -- Clock Reset Unit)
  //    CRU_CLKGATE_CON / CRU_CLKSEL_CON for USB PHY clock

  // 2. De-assert PHY reset
  //    CRU_SOFTRST_CON for USB PHY reset

  // 3. Configure PHY registers at phy_base:
  //    - Set UTMI+ interface parameters
  //    - Configure PLL for 480MHz (HS) or 48MHz (FS)
  //    - Enable VBUS detection
  //    - Set pull-up/pull-down resistors

  // 4. Wait for PHY PLL lock

  // 5. Release PHY to DWC2 controller
}
```

#### 5.2.4 Clock Configuration

```c
// STM32: Clocks are enabled via RCC
// RK3506: Clocks are enabled via CRU (Clock Reset Unit)

static void rk3506_usb_clock_enable(int controller)
{
  // Enable AHB clock for USB OTG controller
  // Enable USB PHY clock (typically 24MHz from oscillator)
  // Enable USB controller clock (480MHz / 48MHz)
  // Configure clock dividers as needed
}
```

#### 5.2.5 Interrupt Configuration

| Item | STM32 | RK3506 |
|------|-------|--------|
| IRQ OTG0 | `STM32_IRQ_OTGFS` | `74` |
| IRQ OTG1 | N/A | `79` |
| IRQ type | GIC (Cortex-M NVIC) | GIC-400 (Cortex-A / RISC-V) |

```c
// In stm32_otgfshost_initialize() equivalent:
irq_attach(74, rk3506_gint_isr, priv);  // OTG0
// or
irq_attach(79, rk3506_gint_isr, priv);  // OTG1
up_enable_irq(74);
```

#### 5.2.6 VBUS Control

STM32 uses HPRT.PPWR and optionally an external GPIO charge pump. RK3506 likely has:
- GPIO-controlled VBUS enable (board-specific)
- Possibly a PMIC regulator

```c
static void rk3506_vbusdrive(struct rk3506_usbhost_s *priv, bool state)
{
  // Control VBUS power via GPIO or PMIC
  // Then set HPRT.PPWR in DWC2
  if (state) {
    gpio_set_value(RK3506_USB_VBUS_GPIO, 1);
    up_mdelay(200);  // Wait for VBUS stabilization
    // Set HPRT.PPWR
  }
}
```

#### 5.2.7 GCCFG Register Differences

The GCCFG (General Core Configuration) register is vendor-specific. STM32 uses:
- `PWRDWN` (bit 16): Power down control
- `VBUSASEN/VBUSBSEN` (bits 18-19): VBUS sensing
- `NOVBUSSENS` (bit 21): Disable VBUS sensing

RK3506's DWC2 may have a different GCCFG layout (Rockchip may add custom bits). Check the RK3506 TRM for the exact GCCFG bit definitions.

#### 5.2.8 Architecture-Specific Concerns (arm32 -> arm64/RISC-V)

From the HCD pattern reference (`usbhost_hcd_pattern.md`, lines 667-678):

1. **Structure alignment**: If targeting arm64, pointer members change from 4 to 8 bytes. Verify `sizeof(struct rk3506_chan_s) % alignment == 0`.
2. **DMA cache flush**: If D-Cache is enabled, all DMA buffers must be flushed before writing DMA addresses to registers. The STM32 driver does NOT do cache management (Cortex-M has no D-Cache). RK3506 (likely Cortex-A or RISC-V with MMU) needs explicit `up_flush_dcache()` calls.
3. **Pointer/integer casts**: Use `(uintptr_t)` intermediate cast for all `(void *)uint32` conversions.
4. **Stack sizes**: Increase to 4096+ for all USB threads on 64-bit architectures.
5. **Format strings**: `size_t` -> `%zu`, `uintptr_t` -> `PRIxPTR`.

- LCD panel: `CONFIG_LCD_SUPPORT_T070S140B=y` for specific panel, PWM backlight

**USB:**
- Config: `CONFIG_USB=y`, `CONFIG_USB_DEVICE=y`, `CONFIG_USB_GADGET=y`, `CONFIG_USBADB=y`
- Init: `sunxi_usb_init()` + `usbdev_adb_initialize()` in late init
- Serial string: `CONFIG_BOARD_USBDEV_SERIALSTR=y`, `usbdev_serialstr_init()`
- ADB: `CONFIG_SYSTEM_ADBD=y` with file/shell/socket/logcat services

**I2C (TWI):**
- Config: `CONFIG_I2C=y`, `CONFIG_R528_TWI0=y`, `CONFIG_R528_TWI2=y`
- Init: `r528_i2c_initialize("/dev/i2cN", port_id)` returns `struct i2c_master_s *`
- Drivers attach to the bus: `gt911_register()`, `shtc3_register()`, `ltr553_register()`, etc.
- Pinmux configured in `sys_config.fex`

**SPI:**
- Config: `CONFIG_DRIVERS_SPI=y`, `CONFIG_SPI_DRIVER=y`
- Init: `sunxi_spibus_initialize(port)` returns `struct spi_dev_s *`
- Used for LCD (`spi_lcd_fb_register`) and potentially other SPI devices

### 8. Key Patterns for RK3506 Port Reuse

**Pattern 1 -- Vendor directory structure:**
```
vendor/<vendor_name>/
├── Make.defs              # Top-level app inclusion (guarded by CUR_FOLDER check)
├── Common.mk              # Shared paths & helper functions
├── chips/<chip_name>/     # Chip-layer (SOC-level code)
│   ├── Make.defs          # Core chip sources, includes ARM arch base
│   ├── drivers/           # HAL drivers (vendor SDK)
│   ├── components/        # Higher-level chip components
│   └── include/           # Chip public headers
├── boards/<chip_name>/    # Board-layer
│   ├── <board_name>/
│   │   ├── Kconfig        # Board selection
│   │   ├── configs/nsh/defconfig
│   │   ├── scripts/Make.defs + linker script
│   │   ├── include/board.h
│   │   └── src/           # Board init code
│   └── drivers/           # Shared board drivers
├── apps/                  # Vendor-specific NuttX apps
└── lichee/ (or equivalent) # Firmware packaging
```

**Pattern 2 -- Build system integration points:**
- `CONFIG_ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM=y` + `CONFIG_ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM_DIR` for board path
- `CONFIG_ARCH_CHIP_CUSTOM=y` + `CONFIG_ARCH_CHIP_CUSTOM_DIR` for chip path
- `Make.defs` at chip level includes `armv7-a/Make.defs` (or `arm64/Make.defs` for AArch64)
- Board `scripts/Make.defs` sets `ARCHSCRIPT`, compiler flags, and `POSTBUILD`
- All HAL includes centralized via `Common.mk` helper functions (`AW_ADD_HAL_INCLUDES`)

**Pattern 3 -- Driver initialization order:**
The `r528_boot.c` / `r528_late_initialize()` pattern is:
1. Early init: CPU frequency, GPIO, perf, watchdog
2. Late init: DMA -> HW spinlock -> PWM -> I2C -> Sensors -> ADC -> NAND -> Display -> Audio -> WiFi/BT -> Crypto

**Pattern 4 -- Binary-only mode support:**
- `CONFIG_ALLWINNER_BINARY_ONLY=y` skips source compilation and links pre-built `.a` libraries
- Board `Makefile` copies pre-built `libboard_allwinner.a` instead of compiling sources
- Useful for proprietary driver blobs (WiFi, BT, audio DSP)

**Pattern 5 -- ROMFS resource packaging:**
- Board `src/Makefile` uses `RCSRCS` (scripts) and `RCRAWS` (raw files) to embed resources
- Resources include: init scripts, audio configs, WiFi firmware, SSH keys, timezone data, media configs

**Pattern 6 -- Multi-image build (AP/TEE/BL/OTA):**
- Same board can build different firmware images via `CONFIG_ARCH_BOARD_CUSTOM_NAME`
- `nsh` = main application, `bl` = bootloader, `tee` = secure world, `ota` = OTA updater
- Each has its own defconfig variant
- POSTBUILD logic branches on the image name to copy to the correct partition slot

# openvela Build

编译 openvela 固件、修改内核配置、运行模拟器。

## 默认目标

默认编译目标为 goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap（64 位 ARM 模拟器）：

```
CONFIG_PATH=vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
OUTPUT_DIR=cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

如果用户指定了其他板级配置路径，替换上述路径即可。

## 命令

### 编译

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

示例：
```bash
./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

**成功标志**: 输出 `#### build completed successfully`

**编译产物**: `<OUTPUT_DIR>/nuttx`（ELF）、`<OUTPUT_DIR>/vela_ap.bin`

### 修改内核配置（menuconfig）

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake menuconfig
```

menuconfig 是交互式 TUI 界面，**不能在 AI 终端中直接运行**。提示用户在自己的终端中执行。

修改配置后保存会自动更新 `.config`。如需持久化到 defconfig：
```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake savedefconfig
```

### 运行模拟器

```bash
./emulator.sh <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

示例：
```bash
./emulator.sh cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

**成功标志**: 出现 `goldfish-armv8a-ap>` NSH 提示符

### 清理编译

The RK3506 chip layer has **3 Critical issues** that must be fixed before merge: a hardware register written with a potentially-NULL framebuffer pointer (VOP), a signed-to-unsigned truncation that silently corrupts error codes (USB host), and an unconditional return that makes a while-loop dead code (USB host enumeration).

---

## Issue List

### DR-001: VOP writes uninitialized fbmem pointer to hardware DMA register [Critical]

- **Dimension**: L1-1 Memory Safety
- **Pattern**: P-01 (NULL pointer dereference)
- **CWE**: CWE-476
- **File**: `rk3506_vop.c:222`
- **Description**: In `rk3506_vop_hwinit()`, the WIN1 DMA start address register (`VOP_WIN1_MST`) is written with `priv->planeinfo.fbmem`. This function is called from `rk3506_vop_register()` at line 343, but `fbmem` is only allocated at line 326 — and the `kmm_zalloc` failure path at line 327 returns before `rk3506_vop_hwinit`. However, `rk3506_vop_hwinit` is called **before** `fb_register_device`, meaning `fbmem` is valid at call time. **BUT**: the `rk3506_vop_hwinit` function is a static helper that writes `priv->planeinfo.fbmem` to hardware at line 222. If the function is ever called independently (e.g., during a power-resume path), `fbmem` could be NULL. The function lacks a NULL guard on `fbmem`.
- **Confidence**: MEDIUM (0.6) — currently safe by call-order, but fragile
- **Fix**: Add a NULL check in `rk3506_vop_hwinit()` before writing the DMA register, or document the precondition with a `DEBUGASSERT(priv->planeinfo.fbmem != NULL)`.

---

### DR-002: VOP casts 64-bit pointer to 32-bit register value [High]

- **Dimension**: L1-5 Type & Numeric Safety
- **Pattern**: P-30 (Pointer truncation on 64-bit)
- **CWE**: CWE-681
- **File**: `rk3506_vop.c:222`
- **Description**: `(uint32_t)(uintptr_t)priv->planeinfo.fbmem` truncates a 64-bit pointer to 32 bits. On an ARM64 build (the RK3506 is Cortex-A7, 32-bit, so this is safe in practice), this would silently lose the upper 32 bits. The cast chain is correct for the target architecture but should use a dedicated macro or be guarded.
- **Confidence**: LOW (0.4) — RK3506 is 32-bit ARM, so this is safe in practice
- **Fix**: Consider using `up_addrenv_va_to_pa()` or a `PHYS_ADDR` macro for clarity, or add a build-time assertion `sizeof(void *) == 4`.

---

### DR-003: Signed error code stored in volatile uint8_t — silent corruption [Critical]

- **Dimension**: L1-5 Type & Numeric Safety
- **Pattern**: P-29 (Signed/unsigned mismatch causing value corruption)
- **CWE**: CWE-681, CWE-195
- **File**: `rk3506_usbhost.c:2455`
- **Description**: In `rk3506_cancel()`, `chan->result = -ESHUTDOWN` assigns a negative value (-108) to `volatile uint8_t result`. The field is `uint8_t` (line 149), so -108 becomes 148 (0x94). Later, in `rk3506_chan_wakeup()` (line 656), the result is checked against `EBUSY` (16). The consumer `rk3506_chan_wait()` at line 642 does `ret = -(int)chan->result` — which would return -148 instead of 108 (ESHUTDOWN). **Every error code is corrupted** because negative errno values are truncated to 8-bit unsigned.
- **Confidence**: HIGH (0.8)
- **Fix**: Change `volatile uint8_t result` to `volatile int result` in `struct rk3506_chan_s` (line 149). This also fixes the general pattern where `chan->result = EIO` etc. are stored — while positive errno values fit in uint8_t, the signed-ness mismatch is a latent bug.

---

### DR-004: Unreachable code after infinite for-loop in ISR [Critical]

- **Dimension**: L1-7 Embedded-Specific
- **Pattern**: P-47 (ISR correctness)
- **CWE**: CWE-561
- **File**: `rk3506_usbhost.c:1907`
- **Description**: `rk3506_gint_isr()` has `for (;;) { ... if (pending == 0) return OK; }` at line 1861-1905. The `return OK` at line 1907 is unreachable dead code. While not a functional bug, it indicates the control flow was not carefully reviewed and may confuse future maintainers or static analyzers.
- **Confidence**: HIGH (0.8)
- **Fix**: Remove the unreachable `return OK;` at line 1907.

---

### DR-005: while-loop with immediate unconditional return — dead loop [High]

- **Dimension**: L1-4 Error Handling
- **Pattern**: P-23 (Logic error in control flow)
- **CWE**: CWE-561
- **File**: `rk3506_usbhost.c:2045-2048`
- **Description**: `rk3506_rh_enumerate()` contains:
  ```c
  while (!priv->connected)
    {
      return -ENODEV;
    }
  ```
  The `while` loop body **always** returns on the first iteration, making the `while` keyword misleading. This should be an `if` statement. The original intent was likely to wait for connection, but the implementation returns immediately.
- **Confidence**: HIGH (0.8)
- **Fix**: Change `while` to `if`:
  ```c
  if (!priv->connected)
    {
      return -ENODEV;
    }
  ```

---

### DR-006: nxmutex_lock return value unchecked in rk3506_epfree [High]

- **Dimension**: L1-4 Error Handling
- **Pattern**: P-22 (Missing return value check)
- **CWE**: CWE-252
- **File**: `rk3506_usbhost.c:2193`
- **Description**: `rk3506_epfree()` calls `nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock)` at line 2193 but does not check the return value. If the lock acquisition fails (e.g., due to signal interruption), the code proceeds to free channels without holding the mutex, causing a data race with concurrent access.
- **Confidence**: HIGH (0.8)
- **Fix**: Check the return value and return early on failure, consistent with the pattern used in `rk3506_epalloc()` (line 2163-2167).

### DR-007: rk3506_chan_freeall uses uint8_t loop counter — type mismatch [Medium]

- **Dimension**: L1-5 Type & Numeric Safety
- **Pattern**: P-28 (Integer type mismatch)
- **CWE**: CWE-190
- **File**: `rk3506_usbhost.c:454`
- **Description**: `rk3506_chan_freeall()` declares `uint8_t chidx` and compares against `RK3506_DWC2_NHOST_CHANNELS` (12). This works correctly for 12 channels, but the loop variable type should match the `int` type used in `rk3506_chan_alloc()` and `rk3506_chan_free()` for consistency. If `RK3506_DWC2_NHOST_CHANNELS` ever exceeds 128, the loop would wrap.
- **Confidence**: HIGH (0.8)
- **Fix**: Change `uint8_t chidx` to `int chidx`.

### DR-008: Buffer pointer alignment not guaranteed in wrpacket [High]

- **Dimension**: L1-6 Input & Boundary Validation
- **Pattern**: P-37 (Alignment assumption)
- **CWE**: CWE-704
- **File**: `rk3506_usbhost.c:1276`
- **Description**: `rk3506_gint_wrpacket()` casts `uint8_t *buffer` to `uint32_t *src` and dereferences it with `*src++`. If the buffer is not 4-byte aligned, this causes an unaligned access exception on ARM (or silent performance penalty on Cortex-A7). The same issue exists in `rk3506_gint_rxflvlisr()` at line 1603.
- **Confidence**: HIGH (0.8)
- **Fix**: Use `memcpy()` to a local `uint32_t` for the copy, or ensure callers always provide aligned buffers. The DWC2 FIFO registers require 32-bit access, so the source must be copied word-by-word safely.

- **Dimension**: L1-8 Design Philosophy
- **Pattern**: DP-07 (Duplicated code / reinventing the wheel)

- **Dimension**: L1-4 Error Handling

### DR-011: VOP setpower/getpower not protected by spinlock [Medium]

- **Dimension**: L1-2 Concurrency Safety
- **Pattern**: P-09 (Data race on shared register state)
- **CWE**: CWE-362
- **File**: `rk3506_vop.c:150-194`
- **Description**: `rk3506_vop_setpower()` and `rk3506_vop_getpower()` perform read-modify-write on `VOP_DSP_CTRL0` without holding the spinlock (`priv->lock`). ### DR-015: DWC2 soft-reset timeout not checked [Medium]

- **Dimension**: L1-7 Embedded-Specific

- **Description**: Both timeout loops in `rk3506_hw_initialize()` (AHB idle wait and core reset) loop up to `RK3506_READY_DELAY` but do not return an error if the timeout expires. The function proceeds as if the reset succeeded, which could leave the controller in an undefined state.

- **Dimension**: L1-7 Embedded-Specific

- **File**: `rk3506_usbhost.c:2052-2064`
- **Description**: `rk3506_rh_enumerate()` calls `rk3506_portreset()` at line 2054, then immediately reads `DWC2_HPRT` to detect speed. # RK3506 Board Layer Driver Code Review

## Critical Issues

### [C1] `board_app_initialize()` does not call `hd_rk3506_bringup()` — peripherals never start

**File**: `hd_rk3506_appinit.c:54-58`
**Severity**: CRITICAL

`board_app_initialize()` is a no-op (returns `OK` without calling `hd_rk3506_bringup()`). Since `CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE` is **not set** in the defconfig, `board_late_initialize()` is also dead code. This means `hd_rk3506_bringup()` is **never called** — the GT911 touchscreen, VOP framebuffer, and USB host are never initialized at runtime.

```c
int board_app_initialize(uintptr_t arg)
{
  return OK;  // BUG: should call hd_rk3506_bringup()
}
```

**Fix**: Either add `CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE=y` to defconfig, or call `hd_rk3506_bringup()` from `board_app_initialize()`:

```c
int board_app_initialize(uintptr_t arg)
{
  return hd_rk3506_bringup();
}
```

---

### [C2] Kconfig missing `CONFIG_INPUT_GT911` option definition

**File**: `Kconfig:1-11`
**Severity**: CRITICAL

The Kconfig only defines `ARCH_BOARD` mapping. The defconfig enables `CONFIG_INPUT_GT911=y`, but this symbol is **never defined** in the board Kconfig. It must come from a chip-level or driver-level Kconfig. If the upstream GT911 driver doesn't define it (it uses a different symbol like `CONFIG_INPUT_GT9XX`), the build will silently skip the GT911 source file and the touchscreen will be non-functional.

**Fix**: Verify the actual Kconfig symbol for the GT911 driver in the chip-level `vendor/rockchip/chips/rk3506/Kconfig` or `nuttx/drivers/input/Kconfig`. The board Kconfig should select or depend on the correct symbol. Consider adding a board-level Kconfig entry:

```kconfig
config INPUT_GT911
    bool "GT911 Touchscreen on I2C0"
    default n
    depends on I2C && INPUT_TOUCHSCREEN
    ---help---
        Enable GT911 capacitive touchscreen on I2C0 (addr 0x5D).
```

---

### [C3] GT911 buffer overflow — `touchpoints * 8` can exceed `GT911_BUFFER_SIZE`

**File**: `hd_rk3506_gt911.c:619-620`
**Severity**: CRITICAL

```c
ret = gt911_read_reg(dev, GT911_READ_DATA_REG,
                     &dev->buffer[1], data->touchpoints * 8);
```

With `GT911_MAX_TOUCH=5`, `5 * 8 = 40` bytes read starting at `buffer[1]` = writes indices 1–40. `GT911_BUFFER_SIZE=41`, so this barely fits. However, the bounds check uses `<= GT911_MAX_TOUCH` (line 615), while the reference ESP32-S3 implementation uses `< GT911_TOUCHPOINTS` (strict less-than). If the hardware reports `touchpoints=5`, this is within bounds, but if it ever reports a corrupted value, there's no margin. The status byte at `buffer[0]` overlaps with the first data byte.

**Fix**: Use strict less-than as in the reference implementation, and add a compile-time assertion:

```c
DEBUGASSERT(data->touchpoints * 8 + 1 <= GT911_BUFFER_SIZE);
```

## High Issues

### [H1] GPIO manipulation bypasses NuttX GPIO framework — no pin mux configuration

**File**: `hd_rk3506_gt911.c:176-259`
**Severity**: HIGH

The driver directly manipulates GPIO registers via `getreg32()`/`putreg32()` instead of using the NuttX GPIO framework (`gpio_*` APIs or `ioctl` on `/dev/gpioN`). This bypasses:
- Pin mux/pad configuration (IOC GRF registers for RK3506)
- GPIO clock gating
- Interrupt configuration for the IRQ pin
- The GPIO subsystem's reference counting and conflict detection

The GPIO register offsets (`GPIO_SWPORTA_DR_L`, etc.) are hardcoded for a specific GPIO controller version. If the RK3506 GPIO controller differs from the assumed layout, the driver will malfunction silently.

**Fix**: Use the NuttX GPIO interface:

```c
#include <nuttx/ioexpander/gpio.h>

// Use gpio_pin_write() and gpio_direction() or open /dev/gpioN
```

Or at minimum, configure the pin mux via the IOC GRF registers for the IRQ and RST pins before accessing GPIO data/direction registers.

### [H2] `spinlock_t lock` declared but never used

**File**: `hd_rk3506_gt911.c:111`
**Severity**: HIGH

The `lock` field is allocated in the device struct but never acquired anywhere. The `gt911_worker()` function accesses `dev->buffer` and `dev->has_report` without any locking. While the LPWORK queue serializes work items, if the driver is ever extended to support interrupt-driven operation or multi-touch, the lack of locking will cause data races.

**Fix**: Either remove the unused `lock` field, or add proper locking around buffer access:

```c
irqstate_t flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&dev->lock);
// ... access shared state ...
spin_unlock_irqrestore(&dev->lock, flags);
```

---

### [H3] Build system inconsistency — CMakeLists.txt vs Makefile ROMFS content

**File**: `Makefile:33-35` vs `CMakeLists.txt:29-40`
**Severity**: HIGH

The **Makefile** only registers ROMFS scripts:
```makefile
RCSRCS = etc/init.d/rc.sysinit etc/init.d/rcS
```

The **CMakeLists.txt** registers scripts AND raw files:
```cmake
nuttx_add_romfs(... RCSRCS etc/init.d/rcS etc/init.d/rc.sysinit RCRAWS etc/group ...)
```

The `etc/group` file exists on disk but is only included in CMake builds. Make-based builds will produce a ROMFS image missing `/etc/group`, which may cause NSH login failures.

**Fix**: Add `etc/group` to the Makefile ROMFS configuration:

```makefile
ifeq ($(CONFIG_ETC_ROMFS),y)
  RCSRCS = etc/init.d/rc.sysinit etc/init.d/rcS
  RCRAWS = etc/group
endif
```
